hypotheses.claim: The council median reduces precipitation error versus the average individual model.
hypotheses.product_update: Keep council median as the default headline.

hypotheses.claim: Higher model disagreement predicts larger forecast error even after normalizing for rainfall magnitude.
hypotheses.effect: normalized corr=0.07; high/low normalized-error ratio=1.10x; heavy-rain corr=-0.26; abstention gain=-12.3%
hypotheses.product_update: Keep disagreement visible, but do not convert it into a confidence penalty yet.

hypotheses.claim: Forecast skill materially degrades from 1 to 3 to 5 days.
hypotheses.product_update: Make forecast horizon a first-class confidence input.

hypotheses.claim: The council median remains useful on heavy-rain days, not only on easy dry days.
hypotheses.product_update: Keep the council as the main heavy-rain summary.

hypotheses.claim: COMMONS should lower confidence when model disagreement is high and lead time is long.
hypotheses.effect: confidence should not yet combine both disagreement and horizon as penalties
hypotheses.product_update: confidence should not yet combine both disagreement and horizon as penalties

hypotheses.claim: Antecedent rainfall and soil moisture improve detection of top-5% discharge days beyond recent 3-day rainfall alone.
hypotheses.effect: mean AUC gain 0.0834; mean precision gain 83.2%
hypotheses.update: Do not apply a global wetness rule. Learn and expose wetness skill per basin.

hypotheses.claim: A revision sustained across multiple lead checkpoints is more useful than a one-off late jump.
hypotheses.effect: persistent direction 97.8%, improvement 70.2%; one-off direction 85.0%, improvement 63.0%
hypotheses.update: Promote sustained multi-checkpoint revisions as a material-change signal.

hypotheses.claim: When at least 2 of 3 models revise in the same direction, that direction is useful for what-changed alerts.
hypotheses.update: Surface "2/3 models revised upward/downward" as a directional change signal.

hypotheses.claim: Current river percentile plus recent trajectory improves detection of an extreme next three days versus current percentile alone.
hypotheses.effect: mean AUC gain -0.0693; mean precision gain -28.5%
hypotheses.update: Keep current river percentile as the primary river-state feature.

hypotheses.claim: A revision-aware material-change rule improves the precision/recall/lead-time trade-off versus fixed forecast thresholds.
hypotheses.effect: F1 gain 0.0134; recall gain 0.0952; precision change -0.0292; lead gain 0.028d
hypotheses.update: Do not replace fixed thresholds with the current revision-aware rule yet.

hypotheses.claim: Separating WATCH from ALERT gains useful recall without materially increasing interruption burden.
hypotheses.effect: alert recall 0.5238; watch recall 0.619; watch-only precision 0.2857; burden 3.48/100d
hypotheses.update: Do not add a separate WATCH tier yet.

hypotheses.claim: Among sub-threshold 3-day forecasts, upward model revisions identify cases that deserve more human attention.
hypotheses.effect: upward-revision heavy-event rate 0.3333 vs 0.0833; lift 0.25; n=12 vs 12
hypotheses.update: Use upward revisions to rank sub-threshold WATCH candidates above otherwise similar cases.

limitations: ERA5 is reanalysis, not a local rain gauge.
Point precipitation is not basin-integrated precipitation.
This evaluates precipitation forecast skill, not human flood impact.
Operational model versions change over time.
The council is a simple median, not a trained probabilistic ensemble.

next_hypotheses.claim: Basin-context rainfall outperforms a single point for river-risk estimation.
next_hypotheses.test: Compare point rainfall with spatially averaged upstream rainfall.

next_hypotheses.claim: We can predict which basins benefit from antecedent-wetness features.
next_hypotheses.test: Cluster basin regimes and validate wetness features out-of-sample.

next_hypotheses.claim: Adding exposure changes which physical hazards deserve human attention first.
next_hypotheses.test: Compare hazard-only ranking with exposure-aware ranking against historical impact records.

next_hypotheses.claim: Official warning changes provide a useful external benchmark for COMMONS attention changes.
next_hypotheses.test: Measure agreement, earlier/later detection and false alarms without treating official warnings as perfect ground truth.

next_hypotheses.claim: A low-cost WATCH layer reduces analyst monitoring time without creating perceived noise.
next_hypotheses.test: Run a human pilot measuring monitoring time, ignored watches, useful catches and perceived interruption burden.
